selection_reason: Coverage-gap analysis + requirement-to-source traceability: the single most transferable discovery mechanism found
mechanism: Ingests multiple unstructured sources (workshop notes, SoWs, stakeholder conversations, project docs) with live intent capture, and links every derived requirement back to its originating source context.
limitations: The '80-90% accuracy' converting SoWs and workshop notes into requirements is a customer testimonial on the vendor's own page, not a measured benchmark. No public detail on how contradictions between two sources are surfaced or adjudicated, nor on what happens when coverage analysis finds a gap.

selection_reason: Only surface in 55 with explicit configurable terminal states — directly answers P01's stopping-rule question
mechanism: Conversational agent on the website asks the same discovery questions a human SDR would, about needs, budget and timeline; simultaneously enriches the conversation with CRM data and real-time research on the visitor's company.
limitations: Public docs do not state how many questions it asks, in what order, or whether ordering adapts to answers. No published accuracy for qualification decisions or false-disqualification rate. Confirmed gap: no automated email follow-up sequences after qualification.

selection_reason: Sharpest precompute/ask boundary: Toggle Fields shown only on enrichment failure (per-field fallback as confidence mechanism)
mechanism: Anonymous visitor de-anonymisation into known accounts, plus Forms Enrichment which supplements a form submission with known company data — populating hidden fields so firmographics are captured without displaying them, and Toggle Fields that stay hidden unless enrichment fails.
limitations: The product page makes no first-party claim about forms enrichment and does not name specific appended fields or the identification methodology — the Toggle Fields and hidden-field mechanics come from Demandbase's support documentation surfaced in search, not from the fetched page. Fill rates are not published.

selection_reason: Closest structural analogue to Actionist: agent sits inside the human discovery call rather than replacing it
mechanism: Agent attends live discovery/refinement calls and ingests institutional knowledge and workshop inputs; unstructured conversation is transformed into structured requirements and kept synced across downstream tools as requirements change.
limitations: getauctor.com returned 403 to fetch; verification is via YC's first-party company profile, not the vendor site. Nothing public establishes extraction accuracy, how contradictions between sessions are resolved, or whether the agent ever asks a clarifying question. The '70% of enterprise implementations experience significant delays' figure is a vendor launch-post claim, unsourced.

selection_reason: Named schema (MEDDIC/BANT) populated by inference from conversation — the exact shape P01 needs; publishes no citations, which is the gap
mechanism: Auto-records and transcribes across conferencing tools with speaker identification in 75+ languages; custom Smart Trackers detect keywords and topics by semantic matching; AI-generated Smart Chapters segment the call by topic.
limitations: The vendor page markets outcomes (4+ hrs/week saved, 40% win-rate lift) without describing the underlying models or, critically, how an extracted MEDDIC field ties back to specific transcript evidence. Whether a filled field carries a citation or a confidence score is not established publicly.

selection_reason: Per-answer confidence scoring plus an explicit model of content decay over time (search-only; needs first-party pass)
mechanism: Inverted discovery: the counterparty asks the questions, and Loopio matches each incoming question against a library of pre-approved answers, importing questionnaires directly from procurement portals.
limitations: Fetch of loopio.com was not completed (model rate limit), so confidence-indicator specifics rest on Loopio's own blog content surfaced via search rather than a fetched product page. The scoring scale, thresholds, and what a low score actually blocks are not established. '1,700 companies' and '61% achieve ROI within a year' are vendor claims from Loopio's own benchmark report.

selection_reason: Narrated reasoning in a channel humans already read, plus pre-execution human approval gate
mechanism: Agentic research with a narrated, inspectable trace surfaced into Slack, and a human approval gate before campaigns launch.
limitations: Not fetched; the Slack narration and approval-gate behaviour is described in SellScale's own published field guide, so it is a first-party claim reached through search rather than a fetched product page. No evidence on how often proposals are rejected.

selection_reason: Category leader retained as a methodological caution: most famous, least mechanism-bearing first-party evidence
mechanism: Automatic capture of calls, emails and meetings across integrated channels; AI analysis over the accumulated interaction corpus, with keyword/topic trackers and methodology scoring layered on top.
limitations: The main product page is notably thin on mechanism: it does not name trackers, next-step extraction, or evidence-structured discovery, and the help-centre tracker doc 404'd. Pricing is unpublished; the $100k-200k/yr for 20-50 seats figure is third-party. Gong's own page establishes marketing positioning far more than it establishes how discovery is structured into evidence.

selection_reason: Accounting-vertical intake with prior-year pre-population then confirmation — industry-specific precompute precedent
mechanism: Workflow templates emitting client requests, with automated follow-up on outstanding documents; integrates with Ignition so a signed proposal auto-creates and assigns the project.
limitations: Not fetched directly; the Ignition integration mechanics are documented first-party by Ignition and by trade press (CPA Practice Advisor, Aug 2025) and are US/Canada only. Karbon's comparison page calling it feature-shallow is a competitor's assessment and should not be treated as fact.

selection_reason: Guided-selling needs-analysis retained as the strongest of a thin 6-row segment
mechanism: Question-based product guides that translate buyer language into catalogue filters.
limitations: Not fetched. Pricing (99 EUR/mo Essential, 599 EUR/mo Plus) is third-party. Small vendor; question-policy depth unestablished.
